summary: Kaiun Shirodate is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He taught at Otani University, where he served as a full-time lecturer (attested 1986–1990) and later as a professor (attested 1999–2002).

Kaj Barr (1896–1970) worked in Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistic studies. He studied at the University of Copenhagen and Göttingen under Arthur Christensen, Poul Tuxen, and Friedrich Carl Andreas, later holding posts at the Royal Danish Academy and Copenhagen.

Kakichi Kadowaki (1926–2017) was a scholar in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and under Sogen Omori, and he held a faculty post at Sophia University from circa 1968 to 1996.

Kakushō Ujiie (d. 1985) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed research study abroad at Tribhuvan University. He held an appointment as professor at Koyasan University, attested in 1970 and from 1984 to 1985.

Kali Kinkar Datta (1905–1982) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as Honorary Director (attested 1959–1966) and Joint Director (attested 1987) of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute, and Vice-Chancellor of Patna University (attested 1973).

Kalidas Nag (1891–1966) specialized in Indology, history, and archaeology. Educated at Scottish Church College, the University of Calcutta, and under Sylvain Lévi, he taught at Scottish Church College (~1915–1919) and the University of Calcutta (~1923–1955).
Kalpana K. Sheth is an Indologist who completed her doctoral studies under Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani. She held a post at the L.D. Institute of Indology.
Kalpana Ram is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the Australian National University (1981–1989) and was attested as holding a post there in 2026.

Kalu Rinpoche (1905–1989) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology master. He studied at Palpung Monastery and Dechen Ösel Ling under several teachers, later serving as Vajra Master at Palpung (~1942–1955) and Abbot at Changchub Choeling Monastery (1957).
Kalyan Kumar Sarkar is a scholar of Indology and sinology who studied under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi. He served as an emeritus professor at the University of Windsor (attested in 2002).
Kamal K. Sridhar is an Indologist and linguist. She served at Stony Brook University, where she was attested as director in 2007 and as Professor Emerita in 2026.

Kamala Tiyavanich specializes in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. She studied at Cornell University under David K. Wyatt, A. Thomas Kirsch, and Richard Polenberg, later holding a Mellon Postdoctoral Fellowship there from 1993 to 1994.

Kamaleswar Bhattacharya (1928–2014) worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held academic posts at Brown University (~1968–1970), the University of Toronto (~1970–1972), and the University of Bonn (~1972–1974).

Kameshwar Nath Mishra works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He held a professorship at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1982–1988, 2001) and was a Visiting Research Scholar at the University of Marburg in 1993.

Kamil Václav Zvelebil (1927–2009) was an Indologist and linguist. After earning his PhD at Charles University under Vincenc Lesný, he held posts at the Oriental Institute (1952–1970), Charles University (~1960–1968), and Utrecht University (~1977–1992).

Kamla Chowdhry (1920–2006) studied at Santiniketan, the University of the Punjab, University of Calcutta (~1943–1945), and Michigan State University (~1947–1949). She held appointments at the Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad (~1962–1972) and Harvard University.

Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Kshetresh Chandra Chattopadhyaya. He served as professor emeritus at Banaras Hindu University, Chairman of the Kalidasa Sanskrit Academy, and Advisor to the IGNCA (attested 2009).

Kammie Takahashi specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Mount Holyoke College and the University of Virginia (PhD ~2002–2009) under David Germano, Paul Groner, and Daishun Ueyama, she held a post at Muhlenberg College in 2011.
Kan Hang (b. 1965) is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Su Bai. He has served as Dean of the School of Archaeology and Museology at Peking University.

Kanai Lal Hazra (b. 1932) is an author in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He earned his PhD at the University of Ceylon under Sirima Kiribamune and later served as Lecturer in Pali at the University of Calcutta (attested 1982).
